name: MAX14919AUP+T
title: Industrial-protected quad-channel low-side switch
summary: Four 140 mΩ (typ) low-side switches for industrial digital outputs, each rated 800 mA, driven directly by four logic pins at up to 500 kHz. One resistor sets a common current limit from 100 mA to 800 mA, with an optional doubled limit for 10 ms at turn-on. Built-in 55 V clamps, short-circuit and thermal protection, ±1 kV/42 Ω surge tolerance and reverse-current detection protect the outputs; a 5 V/30 mA regulator lets the part run from a 7 V to 60 V supply. The MAX14919 shuts all outputs down on reverse current and can drive an external protection MOSFET; the MAX14919A only flags it.
key_figures: 7 V to 60 V on VDD, or 4.5 V to 5.5 V on V5
140 mΩ typ, 300 mΩ max at 600 mA

circuits.title: Simplified low-side switch application
circuits.description: A microcontroller drives IN1 to IN4 directly and reads FAULT back. A 5 V rail feeds both V5 and VL, with one bypass capacitor to ground. Each OUT_ pin sinks the current of one load whose other end sits on a +24 V supply; PGND and GND return to the field ground.
notes: VDD, INRUSH, RCLIM and REV have no connection in this circuit.

circuits.title: Isolated quad-channel digital output with reverse-load polarity protection
circuits.description: A MAX258 transformer driver on the 3.3 V logic rail pushes a 1CT:3CT centre-tapped transformer; two rectifiers and a 1 µF capacitor on the far side give an unregulated field-side rail for VDD of the MAX14919. The part's own 5 V regulator (V5) runs VL and the field side of a MAX14483 digital isolator. Four AND gates on the field side, each fed by one isolator output and the SBA line, drive IN1 to IN4. FAULT goes back through the isolator to the logic side; REV drives the gate of an external n-channel MOSFET (NTTFS5820NLTAG) placed between the chip ground and the field COM terminal. If the load supply is wired backwards and more than 150 mA flows out of an output, REV goes low, the MOSFET turns off and the outputs lose their return path to COM. A 25 kΩ resistor on RCLIM sets the 800 mA current limit, INRUSH is grounded, and a unipolar SMCJ36A TVS across the MOSFET guards it against surge while it is off. The isolator also carries the field-power-ok status to the logic side.

parts.note: centre-tapped transformer; pins P1, PCT, P2 primary, S1, SCT, S2 secondary

notes: The 24 V supply return and COM are tied to earth.
The exposed pad has no connection in this circuit.

circuits.title: Field-isolated quad-channel digital output with MAX14919A
circuits.description: The MAX14919A runs from the 24 V field supply through a series diode into VDD, decoupled by 1 µF. Its 5 V regulator output V5 feeds VL and the field side of a MAX14430EAEE isolator (3 kVRMS), whose ENB is tied high. The isolator's four outputs reach IN1 to IN4 through 33 Ω resistors; the logic-side inputs carry 100 kΩ pull-downs. FAULT and REV each light an LED through a 5.6 kΩ resistor from V5. INRUSH is pulled up to V5 by 10 kΩ, so the doubled inrush limit is on, and 30.1 kΩ on RCLIM sets a 600 mA current limit. The four loads hang between the field supply and OUT1 to OUT4; GND and PGND go to field ground.
notes: The exposed pad has no connection in this circuit.

operation.text: Both versions detect current flowing out of an output when the load supply is reversed. The MAX14919 reacts by switching all outputs off and drives REV to control an external MOSFET for non-capacitive loads; the MAX14919A only reports the event on REV.

Two ways to power the part. From VDD (7 V to 60 V, 24 V typical in industrial systems) the internal low-dropout regulator makes 5 V on V5, so no external converter is needed. With a stable external 5 V available, apply it to V5 (4.5 V to 5.5 V) and ground VDD or leave it open; the regulator is then bypassed. V5 powers the control and analog circuitry in both cases.

V5 can deliver up to 30 mA to outside circuits. At high VDD and high load current the regulator dissipates (VDD − V5) × IV5 and heats the chip, so check the thermal limits at the highest ambient. The regulator has its own temperature sensor and shuts off at 160 °C; it turns back on after the chip cools by 15 °C (typ), a restart hysteresis also given as TCSHDN_HYST (10 °C typ).

VL (1.62 V to 5.5 V) powers the logic interface and sets CMOS logic levels. It can be tied to V5 or fed from 1.8 V or 3.3 V to match a microcontroller, FPGA or digital isolator. Open-drain outputs need pull-up resistors when used and should be grounded when unused.
All switches are held off while VDD, V5 or VL is below its UVLO threshold.

FAULT is a single open-drain flag that goes low on chip thermal shutdown, thermal overload of any switch, reverse current at any output, V5 undervoltage, or a short on RCLIM. It is low during power-up until V5 rises past V5_UVLO. A fault on one channel sets FAULT while the other channels keep working, and FAULT does not depend on the IN_ inputs. It returns high once every switch is back to normal.
While V5 is above V5_UVLO all switches are monitored. Above 150 °C chip temperature (TCSHDN) every output turns off and FAULT is set, until the chip cools below 140 °C (TCSHDN − TCSHDN_HYS).
Each switch has its own sensor. A switch above 160 °C (TJSHDN) turns off alone and comes back once it has cooled by TJSHDN_HYST.

One limit, set between 100 mA and 800 mA by a resistor from RCLIM to GND, applies to all four switches. With RCLIM open or above 650 kΩ the limit defaults to 800 mA; below about 6.5 kΩ all outputs turn off, and RCLIM survives a short. A switch in current limit holds the current at ILIM while its output voltage rises and it heats by VOUT × ILIM; limiting lasts as long as the overload does, or until the input switches the channel off.
With INRUSH high, each switch allows at least twice the RLIM-set current for 10 ms (min) after turn-on, for loads with a large start-up current. After that window the normal limit returns.

Reverse current flows out of an output when a negative voltage appears between OUT_ and GND/PGND, as when the field supply is miswired, whether the switch is on or off. Above 150 mA (typ, ITH_OUT_REV_ON) REV goes low at once. The MAX14919 also turns all four outputs off and holds them off, with REV low, for the 2 s (typ) auto-retry time tREV_AR. It then restores the outputs to their IN_ states and the 45 µA source pulls REV high; if the reverse current is still there the cycle repeats. REV can drive an n-channel MOSFET that disconnects GND/PGND from the field ground/COM and so stops the reverse current.

The MAX14919A has no internal reverse protection. Its REV pin is an open-drain flag that follows the condition live: it goes low while reverse current is detected and releases as soon as it stops, with no 2 s delay, and the outputs stay as set by IN_. It suits an LED or a microcontroller input but not driving a protection MOSFET in the ground path.

Turning on an output into a capacitive load at the end of an inductive cable can ring. If the ringing current exceeds the 150 mA (typ) reverse threshold it counts as reverse current: the MAX14919 then turns all channels off for tREV_AR, while the MAX14919A pulls REV low for as long as it lasts and leaves the outputs alone.

Each output has its own clamp that turns on at 55 V (typ) with respect to PGND to absorb energy from surge, ESD or inductive turn-off, so no external clamp per output is needed in typical use. Larger inductance and current lengthen demagnetization and put more energy into the clamp, heating the chip and possibly setting FAULT through thermal overload; size the load inductance and current so the part is not damaged. Each switch can absorb up to 200 mJ of clamp energy at TJ = +125 °C.

With a switch on and its output shorted to the field supply, the current is regulated to ILIM and the channel heats at VOUT × ILIM. At 160 °C the switch shuts off; after cooling by TJSHDN_HYST it turns back on if its IN_ is still high. It keeps cycling until the input goes low or the short is removed.

Channels can be paralleled for more current by joining both their outputs and their inputs; the current limits add. Paralleled outputs driving an inductive load may need an external Zener clamp per output, with a clamp voltage below the 49 V minimum of the internal clamp.
Every OUT_ withstands IEC 61000-4-5 (1.2 µs/50 µs) surges up to ±1 kV through 42 Ω + 0.5 µF with no external diodes to PGND.

Place supply bypass capacitors as close to the part as possible, with a 1 µF to the ground plane right at VDD. Join PGND and GND with the lowest possible resistance. For heat, solder the exposed pad to a wide ground plane on any layer, and put a dense array of vias under it to carry heat to the lower layers.
